words.enDefinition: A method that starts with an existing budget or actual figures and adjusts them for expected changes.

examples.en: The rehearsal venue used incremental budgeting to allow for higher electricity charges in the coming year.
examples.zh: 排练场馆用「增量预算编制」把下一年可能上升的电费考虑进去。

examples.en: Our case showed how incremental budgeting could carry an unused expense into another planning period.
examples.zh: 案例展示了「增量预算编制」怎样把一项已用不上的支出带入下一个计划期。

collocations: compare incremental budgeting with zero-based budgeting

words.enDefinition: A method requiring activities and expenses to be justified afresh for each budgeting cycle.

examples.en: The student print unit tried zero-based budgeting and reviewed whether it still needed every subscription.
examples.zh: 学生印刷部门尝试「零基预算编制」，重新核查每项订阅是否仍有必要。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how zero-based budgeting would change the way the workshop planned its spending.
examples.zh: 老师问，「零基预算编制」会怎样改变工场规划支出的方式。

words.enDefinition: A method that estimates the activities needed to meet planned demand and budgets for their resources.

examples.en: We used activity-based budgeting to estimate how much time the returns desk would spend checking each batch.
examples.zh: 我们通过「作业基础预算编制」，估算退货服务台检查每批货要花多少时间。

examples.en: The worksheet used activity-based budgeting to turn expected repair orders into planned inspection and testing hours.
examples.zh: 练习表用「作业基础预算编制」把预计维修订单换算成计划检查和测试工时。

words.enDefinition: A method that uses measurable factors, such as bookings or orders, to calculate budget amounts.

examples.en: The example used driver-based budgeting to link packaging costs to the number of parcels shipped.
examples.zh: 示例用「按驱动因素编制预算」的方法，把包装成本与寄出的包裹数量关联起来。

examples.en: Our team used driver-based budgeting so changes in weekly bookings would update the planned desk hours.
examples.zh: 团队「按驱动因素编制预算」，每周预约数一变，服务台的计划工时就会更新。

collocations: apply driver-based budgeting to service costs

words.enDefinition: An approach that involves staff or managers in setting targets they may be responsible for meeting.

examples.en: The case described participative budgeting in which workshop supervisors helped set their own material targets.
examples.zh: 案例介绍了「参与式预算编制」，工场主管会参与设定自己负责的材料目标。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether participative budgeting might improve the accuracy of the printing unit's estimates.
examples.zh: 老师问，「参与式预算编制」是否可能提高印刷部门估算的准确性。

collocations: discuss the benefits of participative budgeting

words.enDefinition: An approach in which lower-level units prepare estimates that are reviewed and combined at higher levels.

examples.en: The university theatre used bottom-up budgeting so each team estimated the costs of its own events.
examples.zh: 大学剧院采用「自下而上的预算编制」，由各团队估算各自的活动成本。

examples.en: With bottom-up budgeting, we combined workshop estimates before discussing the figures with the department manager.
examples.zh: 在「自下而上的预算编制」中，我们先汇总工场的估算，再和部门经理讨论数字。

words.enDefinition: a regularly updated forecast that adds a future period to keep the planning horizon roughly constant

examples.en: The rolling forecast added another month after we entered actual bookings for the month just ended.
examples.zh: 录入刚结束月份的实际预约量后，「滚动预测」又延伸了一个月。

examples.en: We adjusted the rolling forecast after checking the latest repair orders and changes to opening hours.
examples.zh: 核对最新维修订单和开放时间变更后，我们调整了「滚动预测」。

words.enDefinition: Extra room deliberately built into a budget by overstating needs or understating expected performance.

examples.en: The case asked whether the extra labour allowance represented budget slack or a realistic estimate.
examples.zh: 案例问，多留的人工额度是「预算松弛」，还是依据实际情况作出的估算。

examples.en: We looked for budget slack after seeing that all three teams had understated their expected sales.
examples.zh: 我们看到三个团队都低报了预期销售额，便核查是否存在「预算松弛」。

words.enDefinition: A schedule showing when estimates, revisions, reviews, and approvals are due during budget preparation.

examples.en: The budget calendar gave each department a week to revise its figures after the first review.
examples.zh: 「预算编制日程」给各部门留了一周，在初审之后修改数字。

examples.en: We checked the budget calendar before arranging to discuss the workshop's planned purchases with the manager.
examples.zh: 和经理约时间讨论工场计划采购之前，我们先查看了「预算编制日程」。

words.enDefinition: A set of budget figures and supporting information sent to someone for review or approval.

examples.en: Our budget submission included the expected attendance and the cost of running each student workshop.
examples.zh: 我们「提交的预算材料」包括预计到场人数和举办每场学生工作坊的成本。

examples.en: The manager returned the budget submission because one page omitted the assumptions about weekend staffing.
examples.zh: 有一页没写周末人手安排的假设，经理退回了「提交的预算材料」。

words.enDefinition: Instructions or assumptions given to the people preparing budgets so they use a consistent basis.

examples.en: The budget guidance asked every workshop to explain any increase in expected material usage next year.
examples.zh: 「预算编制指引」要求各工场解释下一年预计材料用量增加的原因。

examples.en: Our group checked the budget guidance before estimating how much power the new printer would use.
examples.zh: 估算新打印机的用电量前，我们小组先看了「预算编制指引」。

words.enDefinition: Estimates or assumptions about future conditions used to construct the budget.

examples.en: The budget assumptions included similar ticket demand on both weekends, even though the sessions differed.
examples.zh: 「预算编制假设」包括，尽管两个周末的场次不同，门票需求大致相同。

examples.en: We recorded our budget assumptions before asking the coordinator to check the planned staffing costs.
examples.zh: 请协调员核对计划人员成本前，我们记录了「预算编制假设」。

words.enDefinition: A stated level of revenue, cost, or other performance to be achieved under a budget.

examples.en: The finance team set a budget target for postage based on the mailing schedule for the term.
examples.zh: 财务团队根据本学期的邮寄安排，设定了邮费「预算目标」。

examples.en: We compared the actual repairs completed with the budget target for the workshop's first month.
examples.zh: 我们把实际完成的维修量与工场首月的「预算目标」作了比较。

words.enDefinition: The budget initially set for a period, used as a reference when analysing revisions or results.

examples.en: The original budget assumed both repair desks would remain open throughout the autumn term.
examples.zh: 「最初的预算」假设两个维修服务台整个秋季学期都会开放。

examples.en: We used the original budget as a reference when reviewing the updated estimates for next month.
examples.zh: 审查下月更新的估算时，我们以「最初的预算」为参考。

words.enDefinition: An updated budget reflecting changes to its assumptions, figures, or approved plans after it was first prepared.

examples.en: The revised budget allowed for fewer event sessions after the hall became unavailable on Fridays.
examples.zh: 大厅周五无法使用后，「修订后的预算」按更少的活动场次编制。

examples.en: Our tutor showed how a revised budget could account for a known change in fuel costs.
examples.zh: 老师演示了「修订后的预算」可以怎样纳入已知的燃料费用变化。

collocations: compare figures with the revised budget

words.enDefinition: a limit on how much spending may be included in or authorised under a budget for a unit or purpose

examples.en: The workshop's budget ceiling limited how much the student team could plan to spend on tools.
examples.zh: 工场的「预算支出上限」限制了学生团队可以为工具编列多少费用。

examples.en: We checked the budget ceiling before choosing which repairs to include in the next period.
examples.zh: 确定下一期包含哪些维修之前，我们先核对了「预算支出上限」。

words.enDefinition: A meeting to examine a budget proposal or figures and discuss any changes needed.

examples.en: At the budget review meeting, two departments explained why their staffing estimates had changed.
examples.zh: 在「预算审查会议」上，两个部门解释了人手估算为什么变了。

examples.en: We brought the sales assumptions to the budget review meeting so the group could check them.
examples.zh: 我们把销售假设带到「预算审查会议」上，让小组核对。

collocations: prepare for the budget review meeting
present figures at a budget review meeting

words.enDefinition: A temporary restriction on changing budgets or authorising additional spending, depending on the organisation's rules.

examples.en: The example department faced a budget freeze while administrators reviewed spending on the new equipment.
examples.zh: 管理人员审查新设备支出期间，例子中的部门面临「预算冻结」。

examples.en: The supervisor explained which routine purchases could still go ahead during the temporary budget freeze.
examples.zh: 主管解释了临时「预算冻结」期间，哪些日常采购仍然可以进行。

collocations: review the effect of a budget freeze

words.enDefinition: A budget schedule showing when cash from sales or other receivables is expected to be collected.

examples.en: The cash collections schedule showed that some June sales would only be collected in July.
examples.zh: 「预计现金收款明细表」显示，六月的部分销售款要到七月才收得到。

examples.en: We used the cash collections schedule to estimate how much money was available for the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们用「预计现金收款明细表」估算有多少资金可以给工场使用。

words.enDefinition: A budget schedule showing when cash is expected to be paid for purchases and other expenses.

examples.en: The cash payments schedule listed the equipment deposit in May and the balance in July.
examples.zh: 「预计现金付款明细表」把设备订金列在五月，尾款列在七月。

examples.en: The team updated its cash payments schedule after the supplier changed the date on its invoice.
examples.zh: 供应商改了账单日期后，团队更新了「预计现金付款明细表」。

words.enDefinition: The amount by which planned cash payments exceed the resources available before any new financing.

examples.en: We found a cash shortfall before financing when the equipment bill came due before ticket receipts.
examples.zh: 设备款先到期，票款还未到账，因此我们发现了「融资前现金缺口」。

examples.en: We marked the cash shortfall before financing on the worksheet before adding the planned borrowing.
examples.zh: 我们先在练习表上标出「融资前现金缺口」，再加上计划借入的金额。

collocations: calculate the cash shortfall before financing
show a cash shortfall before financing
compare the cash shortfall before financing

words.enDefinition: The projected period-end cash after nonfinancing receipts and payments, before borrowing or other financing flows.

examples.en: We calculated the cash balance before financing by adding receipts and subtracting payments from the opening balance.
examples.zh: 我们从期初余额加上收款、扣除付款，求出「融资前现金余额」。

examples.en: The case compared the cash balance before financing with the minimum balance the bookshop wanted to maintain.
examples.zh: 案例把「融资前现金余额」与书店想保持的最低余额作了比较。

collocations: calculate the cash balance before financing
show the cash balance before financing
compare the cash balance before financing with the target

words.enDefinition: The expected cash at the end of a budget period after planned receipts, payments and any financing cash flows.

examples.en: The budgeted ending cash balance for June became the starting figure in the next month's worksheet.
examples.zh: 六月的「预计期末现金余额」成为下个月练习表的期初数字。

examples.en: We checked the budgeted ending cash balance after subtracting the planned payment for the new projector.
examples.zh: 扣除计划支付的新投影仪款后，我们核对了「预计期末现金余额」。

collocations: calculate the budgeted ending cash balance
carry forward the budgeted ending cash balance
check the budgeted ending cash balance

words.enDefinition: A target amount of cash that an organisation wants to retain at the end of a period.

examples.en: The exercise required a minimum cash balance even after the workshop paid its suppliers in June.
examples.zh: 练习要求工场在六月向供应商付款后仍保持「最低现金储备余额」。

examples.en: Our group compared the expected ending cash with the minimum cash balance set by the committee.
examples.zh: 我们小组把预计期末现金与委员会设定的「最低现金储备余额」作了比较。

collocations: compare ending cash with the minimum cash balance

words.enDefinition: The number of units that the organisation expects to sell in the budget period.

examples.en: We multiplied budgeted unit sales by the expected price to estimate revenue for the print stall.
examples.zh: 我们把「预算销量」乘以预计价格，估算印刷摊位的收入。

examples.en: The team reduced budgeted unit sales after learning that one branch would close during the holidays.
examples.zh: 得知一个分点假期会关闭后，团队调低了「预算销量」。

words.enDefinition: The selling price assumed for one unit when preparing the sales budget.

examples.en: The budgeted selling price stayed unchanged when the student group revised its estimate of ticket sales.
examples.zh: 学生小组更新门票销量估计值时，「预算销售单价」仍保持原值。

examples.en: We compared the budgeted selling price with what customers actually paid during the sample period.
examples.zh: 我们把「预算销售单价」与示例期间顾客实际支付的单价作了比较。

collocations: compare actual prices with the budgeted selling price

words.enDefinition: The number of units to be made during a period according to the production plan or budget.

examples.en: We calculated planned production units before estimating how much paper the print shop would need.
examples.zh: 我们先算出「计划生产数量」，再估算印刷店需要多少纸。

examples.en: The case increased planned production units because the workshop wanted more finished stock by June.
examples.zh: 案例提高了「计划生产数量」，因为工场想在六月前备好更多成品库存。

collocations: use planned production units in the materials budget

words.enDefinition: The quantity of stock planned to be on hand at the end of a budget period.

examples.en: We added desired ending inventory to expected sales before subtracting the stock already available at opening.
examples.zh: 我们把「目标期末存货」加到预期销量上，再减去期初已有的库存。

examples.en: The plan raised desired ending inventory just before the term because demand was expected to rise.
examples.zh: 开学后需求预计会上升，所以计划提高了开学前的「目标期末存货」。

words.zhGloss: 按实际业务量调整预算
words.enDefinition: To recalculate budget amounts at actual activity using the planned cost and revenue relationships.
acceptedZhAnswers: 按实际业务量调整预算

examples.en: We had to flex the budget after actual production differed from the original plan that month.
examples.zh: 当月实际产量和原计划不同时，我们得「按实际业务量调整预算」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to flex the budget without replacing the budgeted rate with the actual rate.
examples.zh: 老师请我们「按实际业务量调整预算」，仍使用预算费率。

collocations: flex the budget to actual activity
flex the budget before comparing costs
ask someone to flex the budget

words.zhGloss: 实际结果与静态预算的差异
words.enDefinition: The difference between actual results and the original budget at its planned activity level.
acceptedZhAnswers: 实际结果与静态预算的差异

examples.en: The static-budget variance included the effects of both selling fewer units and charging a lower price.
examples.zh: 「实际结果与静态预算的差异」包含销量减少和实际售价较低这两方面的影响。

examples.en: We broke the static-budget variance into two parts to see how much came from sales volume.
examples.zh: 我们把「实际结果与静态预算的差异」分成两部分，看其中多少来自销量。

collocations: compare the static-budget variance with its components

words.zhGloss: 实际结果与弹性预算的差异
words.enDefinition: The difference between an actual result and the budgeted amount restated for the actual activity level.
acceptedZhAnswers: 实际结果与弹性预算的差异

examples.en: We compared actual spending with the amount allowed at actual activity to find the flexible-budget variance.
examples.zh: 我们对比实际支出和按实际业务量计算的允许金额，求出「实际结果与弹性预算的差异」。

examples.en: The flexible-budget variance remained after we allowed for the higher number of orders actually processed.
examples.zh: 按实际处理的更多订单量调整后，仍存在「实际结果与弹性预算的差异」。

words.enDefinition: The difference between the flexible and original budgets caused by a change in activity level.

examples.en: The activity variance showed what changed when we used the actual number of workshops in the budget.
examples.zh: 「业务量差异」说明了，预算改用实际工作坊场次后会有什么变化。

examples.en: Our tutor calculated the activity variance before comparing actual spending with the budget at actual activity.
examples.zh: 老师先算了「业务量差异」，再把实际支出和按实际业务量编制的预算比较。

collocations: separate the activity variance from spending effects

words.enDefinition: A cost or efficiency standard based on conditions with no normal waste, delays, or interruptions.

examples.en: The workbook's ideal standard assumed the printing press would run without any setup time or wasted paper.
examples.zh: 练习册的「理想标准」假设印刷机运行时无需调机，也不会浪费纸张。

examples.en: Our tutor used an ideal standard to show what the assembly line could achieve under perfect conditions.
examples.zh: 老师用「理想标准」说明装配线在完美条件下能达到什么水平。

collocations: compare an ideal standard with a practical standard

words.enDefinition: A demanding standard that allows for normal losses and interruptions under efficient operating conditions.

examples.en: The students set a practical standard that allowed time to clean the mixer between batches of dough.
examples.zh: 学生设定了「可实现标准」，给每批面团之间的搅拌机清洁留出时间。

examples.en: A practical standard still challenged our team, even though it allowed a small amount of unavoidable waste.
examples.zh: 虽然允许少量不可避免的浪费，「可实现标准」对我们组仍有挑战性。

collocations: allow for downtime in a practical standard

words.enDefinition: The planned cost per unit of material used to calculate standard material costs and variances.

examples.en: We used the standard material price for card stock when we calculated the planned cost per folder.
examples.zh: 计算每个文件夹的计划成本时，我们用了卡纸的「标准材料单价」。

examples.en: The standard material price remained unchanged throughout the exercise even after the supplier quoted a different amount.
examples.zh: 整个练习期间供应商报了另一个价格，但「标准材料单价」始终未变。

collocations: compare with the standard material price

words.zhGloss: 单位产品标准材料用量
words.enDefinition: The planned material needed to make one finished unit under the conditions used in the standard.
acceptedZhAnswers: 单位产品标准材料用量

examples.en: The standard material quantity per unit included the small strips of fabric removed during normal trimming.
examples.zh: 「单位产品标准材料用量」包含正常裁剪中切掉的少量布条。

examples.en: We multiplied the standard material quantity per unit by the number of notebooks that passed inspection.
examples.zh: 我们把「单位产品标准材料用量」乘以通过检查的笔记本数量。

collocations: set the standard material quantity per unit
check the standard material quantity per unit
multiply the standard material quantity per unit by output

words.enDefinition: The planned labour cost per hour for a given activity or worker category.

examples.en: The tutor gave us a standard labour rate for the technicians who assembled the practice kits.
examples.zh: 老师给出了组装练习套件的技工的「标准人工费率」。

examples.en: We used the standard labour rate to put a monetary value on the additional assembly hours.
examples.zh: 我们用「标准人工费率」把额外的装配工时换算成金额。

collocations: value hours at the standard labour rate
compare actual pay with the standard labour rate

words.zhGloss: 实际产量对应的标准工时
words.enDefinition: The labour or activity hours that should be needed for the actual output at the standard time per unit.
acceptedZhAnswers: 实际产量对应的标准工时

examples.en: The standard hours allowed rose because the workshop completed more repair kits than the original budget assumed.
examples.zh: 工场完成的维修套件比原预算预计的多，因此「实际产量对应的标准工时」也增加了。

examples.en: We compared the standard hours allowed with the hours recorded for the same batch of finished aprons.
examples.zh: 我们用「实际产量对应的标准工时」对比同一批成品围裙所记录的工时。

collocations: compare actual hours with standard hours allowed
the standard hours allowed for actual output

words.zhGloss: 实际产量对应的标准用量
words.enDefinition: The amount of input allowed by the standard for the number of finished units actually produced.
acceptedZhAnswers: 实际产量对应的标准用量

examples.en: In the bakery case, the standard quantity allowed depended on how many rolls passed the quality check.
examples.zh: 在烘焙店案例中，「实际产量对应的标准用量」取决于有多少面包卷通过质检。

examples.en: Actual fabric use exceeded the standard quantity allowed for the number of bags the class produced.
examples.zh: 针对全班实际做出的包数，实际布料用量超出「实际产量对应的标准用量」。

collocations: use less than the standard quantity allowed
value the standard quantity allowed at standard price

words.enDefinition: the number of hours paid for under a labour cost calculation, including paid idle hours if present

examples.en: The actual hours paid included twenty minutes when the class technicians were waiting for replacement parts.
examples.zh: 「实际付薪工时」包含课堂案例里的技工等待替换零件的二十分钟。

examples.en: The wage record showed the actual hours paid, while a separate sheet recorded time spent assembling units.
examples.zh: 工资记录显示「实际付薪工时」，另一张表则记着花在组装产品上的时间。

collocations: compare actual hours paid with hours worked
use actual hours paid to calculate the hourly rate

words.enDefinition: The amount of material consumed during the production or activity being measured.

examples.en: Our worksheet compared the actual material quantity used with the allowance for the same number of signs.
examples.zh: 练习表把「实际材料用量」与同等数量标牌对应的标准用量作比较。

examples.en: We weighed the leftover dough to check the actual material quantity used in the morning batch.
examples.zh: 我们称了剩余面团，以核对早晨这批产品的「实际材料用量」。

collocations: record the actual material quantity used
measure the actual material quantity used
compare the actual material quantity used with the standard

words.enDefinition: The number of units of an input bought during the period, whether already used or still on hand.

examples.en: The actual quantity purchased was higher than production use because the workshop kept some fabric for next month.
examples.zh: 「实际采购量」高于生产用量，因为工场留了一些布料到下个月用。

examples.en: Use the actual quantity purchased for this price calculation, including the wood still in the storeroom.
examples.zh: 这道价格计算题用「实际采购量」，也就是把仍在库房的木材算进去。

collocations: the actual quantity purchased during the month
multiply the actual quantity purchased by the price difference

words.enDefinition: The cost per unit actually paid or charged for the material in the calculation.

examples.en: The case included freight in the actual material price because it was part of acquiring the fabric.
examples.zh: 案例把运费计入「实际材料单价」，因为那是购入布料的一部分成本。

examples.en: After the second invoice arrived, the class calculated the actual material price per sheet of card stock.
examples.zh: 第二张发票到后，同学们计算了每张卡纸的「实际材料单价」。

collocations: compare the actual material price with the standard
the actual material price per kilogram

words.enDefinition: The labour cost actually incurred per hour for the hours and workers being compared.

examples.en: The actual labour rate went up when the workshop assigned a more experienced technician to the repairs.
examples.zh: 工场派更有经验的技工来维修后，「实际人工费率」提高了。

examples.en: We divided wage cost by paid hours to find the actual labour rate for the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 我们用工资成本除以付薪工时，得出了课堂练习里的「实际人工费率」。

collocations: an actual labour rate above standard
multiply the actual labour rate by actual hours

examples.en: We had to reconcile actual to budget before presenting the print room's monthly figures to our tutor.
examples.zh: 向老师汇报印刷室的月度数字前，我们得「核对并解释实际与预算的差额」。

examples.en: To reconcile actual to budget, we listed each price change and each shift in production volume.
examples.zh: 为了「核对并解释实际与预算的差额」，我们列出了每次价格变动和每次产量变化。

collocations: reconcile actual to budget by category
reconcile actual to budget each month
reconcile actual to budget using a variance bridge

words.enDefinition: A document that shows differences between actual figures and a budget or standard, sometimes with explanations.

examples.en: The variance report showed that paper costs were on plan but overtime costs were higher than expected.
examples.zh: 「差异报告」显示纸张成本符合计划，但加班成本高于预期。

examples.en: Our tutor asked for a variance report that separated price changes from changes in quantities sold.
examples.zh: 老师要求提交一份把价格变化和销量变化分开列示的「差异报告」。

collocations: add commentary to a variance report

words.enDefinition: A written explanation of the main differences identified in a comparison with budget or standard.

examples.en: The variance commentary linked the higher printing cost to a small batch that needed special paper.
examples.zh: 「差异说明」指出印刷成本偏高是因为有一小批产品用了特种纸。

examples.en: Our group kept the variance commentary short and referred readers to the calculation for each figure.
examples.zh: 我们小组把「差异说明」写得简短，并提醒读者查每个数字对应的计算。

collocations: add variance commentary to the report

words.enDefinition: The part of a change in revenue or cost attributed to a difference in the price per unit.

examples.en: The worksheet isolated the price effect by keeping the number of tickets sold the same in both columns.
examples.zh: 练习表把两列售出的票数保持一致，以单独量化「价格效应」。

examples.en: We found a strong price effect after the supplier charged more for an otherwise unchanged order.
examples.zh: 其他订单条件都没变，供应商涨价后，我们观察到明显的「价格效应」。

collocations: separate the price effect from changes in volume

words.enDefinition: The portion of a change in a total caused by a change in the amount sold, bought or produced.

examples.en: The workshop's costs rose mainly because of the volume effect after it produced an extra batch of folders.
examples.zh: 工场多做了一批文件夹，成本上涨主要来自「数量效应」。

examples.en: We held the ticket price constant while estimating the volume effect for the two rehearsal dates.
examples.zh: 为了估算两个排练日期的「数量效应」，我们把票价设为不变。

collocations: label the volume effect in a variance bridge

words.enDefinition: The change in a total caused by different proportions of products or inputs at a given overall quantity.

examples.en: The mix effect explained why contribution rose even though the stall sold the same total number of mugs.
examples.zh: 摊位卖出的杯子总数不变，而「组合效应」解释了边际贡献为什么会上升。

examples.en: We isolated the mix effect before calculating what the higher total input had cost the bakery.
examples.zh: 我们先单独量化「组合效应」，再计算总投入增加让烘焙店多花了多少钱。

collocations: separate the mix effect from total volume

words.enDefinition: To divide a difference into components showing the individual changes that account for it.

examples.en: The tutor asked us to break down a variance instead of giving the class one unexplained total.
examples.zh: 老师让我们「分解差异」，别只给全班一个没有解释的总数。

examples.en: To break down a variance, our group needed sales quantities and the unit price for each product.
examples.zh: 要「分解差异」，我们组需要每件商品的销量和单价。

collocations: break down a variance by product
break down a variance into price and volume
break down a variance for the report

words.enDefinition: Two or more variances with opposing effects that reduce the effect of one another when combined.

examples.en: The small total hid offsetting variances from cheaper fabric and extra fabric used in the workshop.
examples.zh: 总差异看起来很小，却掩盖了布料变便宜和工场布料用量增加形成的「相互抵消的差异」。

examples.en: Our tutor wanted offsetting variances shown separately so the class could see what happened in each department.
examples.zh: 老师希望分别列出「相互抵消的差异」，让大家了解各个部门发生了什么。

words.enDefinition: The overall difference after favourable and adverse components have been combined with the appropriate signs.

examples.en: The net variance was close to zero because lower paint prices almost cancelled the cost of extra paint.
examples.zh: 油漆降价几乎抵消了多耗油漆的成本，因此「净差异」接近零。

examples.en: We calculated the net variance after checking which lines were favourable and which ones were adverse.
examples.zh: 我们核对了哪些行是有利差异、哪些是不利差异，再计算「净差异」。

collocations: reconcile the components to the net variance

words.expression: variance as a percentage of budget
words.lemma: variance as a percentage of budget
words.enDefinition: the difference between actual and budgeted amounts expressed as a percentage of the budgeted amount when that amount is nonzero
acceptedEnVariants: variance as a percentage of budget

examples.en: The tutor asked us to show each variance as a percentage of budget alongside its amount in dollars.
examples.zh: 老师让我们在每项差异的美元金额旁注明该项「差异占预算的百分比」。

examples.en: Showing variance as a percentage of budget made the two workshops easier to compare.
examples.zh: 列出「差异占预算的百分比」后，就更容易比较两间工场的数据。

collocations: calculate a variance as a percentage of budget
report a variance as a percentage of budget
compare each variance as a percentage of budget

words.enDefinition: The effect of a change in the number of units sold on revenue, valued at the budgeted selling price.
acceptedZhAnswers: 按售价计算的销量差异

examples.en: The sales volume revenue variance was adverse because fewer tickets sold, even though ticket prices stayed unchanged.
examples.zh: 门票价格没变，但售出的票数减少，因此「销量收入差异」不利。

examples.en: We multiplied the difference in units sold by the budgeted price to find the sales volume revenue variance.
examples.zh: 我们用实际与预算销量的差额乘以预算单价，算出「销量收入差异」。

collocations: calculate the sales volume revenue variance
an adverse sales volume revenue variance
separate the sales volume revenue variance from the price effect

words.enDefinition: Describing a cost result below the relevant budget or standard at the basis being used for comparison.

examples.en: The case was favourable on cost because the fabric charge was lower at the same production volume.
examples.zh: 案例在相同产量下的布料支出更低，所以结果「成本方面有利」。

examples.en: The printing job looked favourable on cost until we noticed that the team had produced fewer leaflets.
examples.zh: 我们发现团队少印了传单，才知道这项印刷工作表面上「成本方面有利」。

collocations: favourable on cost but behind on volume
favourable on cost against the flexible budget

words.enDefinition: A major factor that explains why an actual figure differs from its budget or standard.

examples.en: The class identified discounted ticket prices as the main variance driver after checking attendance for both performances.
examples.zh: 全班核对了两场演出的到场人数后，把票价打折确定为「差异的主要成因」。

examples.en: The workshop report treated poor fabric yield as a variance driver and explained its effect on unit costs.
examples.zh: 工场报告把布料出成率低列为「差异的成因」，并解释了它对单位成本的影响。

collocations: explain a variance driver in the report

words.enDefinition: The review of a reported variance to verify it and determine what caused it.

examples.en: The variance investigation began when the electricity charge for the practice workshop rose without a change in hours.
examples.zh: 练习工场工时未变，电费却上涨，于是开始了「差异调查」。

examples.en: A variance investigation revealed that two batches of cups had been counted in the wrong month.
examples.zh: 「差异调查」发现，有两批杯子被算进了错误的月份。

words.enDefinition: An accounting approach that reports results by organisational unit and links measures to what its manager can influence.

examples.en: Our course used responsibility accounting to decide which results belonged in each workshop manager's monthly report.
examples.zh: 课程用「责任会计」确定各工场经理的月度报告应涵盖哪些经营结果。

examples.en: The responsibility accounting exercise gave the library team control over supplies while central office managed rent.
examples.zh: 「责任会计」练习中，图书馆团队负责物资开支，总部负责租金。

collocations: evaluate a unit through responsibility accounting

words.enDefinition: An organisational unit whose manager is accountable for specified results and has authority over decisions affecting those results.

examples.en: The campus print room became a responsibility centre with its own budget and a named manager.
examples.zh: 校园印刷室成了「责任中心」，有自己的预算，也指定了一名经理负责。

examples.en: Our tutor asked what decisions the manager of each responsibility centre could actually make in the case.
examples.zh: 老师问，案例中每个「责任中心」的经理实际能做哪些决定。

collocations: assign a manager to a responsibility centre

words.enDefinition: A responsibility centre whose manager is assessed mainly on revenue and has primary authority over generating it.

examples.en: The booking desk was a revenue centre because its manager was evaluated on the revenue from ticket sales.
examples.zh: 售票处经理的考核指标是门票收入，因此售票处属于「收入中心」。

examples.en: Our tutor treated the campus studio's sales team as a revenue centre for the reporting exercise.
examples.zh: 老师在报告练习中把校园工作室的销售团队视作「收入中心」。

collocations: evaluate a revenue centre on sales
classify a unit as a revenue centre

words.enDefinition: A responsibility centre whose manager is accountable for profit and the capital invested in the unit.

examples.en: The workshop was an investment centre because its manager oversaw profits and could approve equipment purchases.
examples.zh: 工场经理负责利润，也有权批准设备采购，因此工场是「投资中心」。

examples.en: We compared the profit and invested capital of each investment centre in the final classroom report.
examples.zh: 在课堂最后的报告中，我们比较了各「投资中心」的利润和投入资本。

collocations: the assets of an investment centre

words.enDefinition: A cost centre where there is no readily measurable relationship between expenditure and the value or volume of output.

examples.en: Our tutor used the training office as a discretionary cost centre because useful outcomes were hard to measure.
examples.zh: 老师把培训办公室当作「酌量性成本中心」，因为有价值的成果很难量化。

examples.en: The case assessed a discretionary cost centre using its budget and the quality of service it provided.
examples.zh: 案例根据预算和服务质量来评价这个「酌量性成本中心」。

collocations: budget for a discretionary cost centre

words.enDefinition: An internal report showing the performance measures and budget differences assigned to a particular manager or responsibility centre.

examples.en: The responsibility report separated the maintenance team's supply costs from building charges set by central office.
examples.zh: 「责任会计报告」把维修团队领用物资的成本和总部定下的楼宇费用分开。

examples.en: In our case, each manager received a responsibility report for the department they could actually influence.
examples.zh: 案例中，每位经理收到的「责任会计报告」都对应自己实际有权管理的部门。

collocations: show controllable costs in the responsibility report

words.enDefinition: The principle that a manager's performance should be assessed on factors they can substantially influence.

examples.en: The controllability principle led our tutor to exclude building rent when assessing the workshop supervisor's performance.
examples.zh: 按「可控性原则」，老师评估工场负责人的表现时剔除了房租。

examples.en: The class discussed how the controllability principle applied when a supplier changed prices across the organisation.
examples.zh: 全班讨论了供应商面向整个机构调价时，怎样应用「可控性原则」。

collocations: use the controllability principle in performance evaluation

words.enDefinition: A measure of divisional profit based on revenue and costs that the division manager can influence.

examples.en: The class calculated controllable profit before adding charges that the print room manager had no authority over.
examples.zh: 全班先算「可控利润」，然后再纳入印刷室经理无权决定的收费项目。

examples.en: The case used controllable profit to review the manager's decisions about prices, staffing and local supplies.
examples.zh: 案例用「可控利润」评估经理在定价、人员和当地物资采购方面的决策。

collocations: evaluate a manager using controllable profit
compare controllable profit with traceable profit

words.enDefinition: Divisional revenue less costs attributable directly to that division, whether or not its manager controls them.

examples.en: We included rent paid specifically for the workshop in traceable profit even though headquarters signed the lease.
examples.zh: 租约虽由总部签订，但工场专用场地的租金仍纳入「可归属利润」的计算。

examples.en: In the case, traceable profit excluded the central office costs shared by all three regional units.
examples.zh: 案例里的「可归属利润」没有扣除由三个地区部门分摊的总部成本。

collocations: compare traceable profit with controllable profit

words.enDefinition: The profit reported for a division, which can include a share of central costs depending on the reporting basis.

examples.en: The tutor showed why divisional profit fell when the exercise allocated more of the central costs there.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么练习把更多总部成本分摊给这个事业部后，「事业部利润」会下降。

examples.en: Our case showed divisional profit after shared office costs and listed the earlier traceable result separately.
examples.zh: 案例列出了扣除分摊总部费用后的「事业部利润」，并把前面算出的可归属利润单独列出。

collocations: report divisional profit after central charges
reconcile divisional profit to the segment report

words.enDefinition: A cost directly attributable to a specific segment, whether or not the segment manager controls it.

examples.en: The standalone studio lease was a traceable cost of the recording unit even though central office negotiated it.
examples.zh: 独立录音室的租约虽由总部谈妥，相关租金还是录音部门的「可归属成本」。

examples.en: In our case, the projector rental was a traceable cost of the short course that used it.
examples.zh: 案例中，投影仪租金是使用它的短期课程的「可归属成本」。

collocations: assign a traceable cost to a division
treat rent as a traceable cost

words.enDefinition: A difference caused by a factor outside the relevant manager's practical authority during the period being assessed.

examples.en: The case recorded an uncontrollable variance when the landlord changed a charge the unit manager could not influence.
examples.zh: 房东改了一项部门经理无法左右的收费，案例将其列为「不可控差异」。

examples.en: Our group labelled the central wage adjustment an uncontrollable variance for the local manager in the exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习中，我们组把总部调整工资产生的差异列为当地经理的「不可控差异」。

words.enDefinition: Being answerable for commitments and results within an assigned budget and for explaining departures from it.

examples.en: Budget accountability in the case meant explaining unexpected expenses and showing how the team used its allocation.
examples.zh: 案例里的「预算问责」要求解释意外支出，并说明团队如何使用分配到的经费。

examples.en: The tutor asked how budget accountability would work when two departments used the same pool of funds.
examples.zh: 老师问，两个部门使用同一笔经费时，如何落实「预算问责」。

collocations: define budget accountability for each unit

words.enDefinition: A comparison of reported results with the figures planned in the budget.

examples.en: The workbook tracked performance against budget for both product sales and the workshop's monthly supply costs.
examples.zh: 练习册跟踪产品销售和工场月度物料成本的「预算执行表现」。

examples.en: Our group assessed performance against budget before discussing whether the original attendance estimate had been realistic.
examples.zh: 我们组先评估「预算执行表现」，再讨论最初的人数估计是否现实。

collocations: a report on performance against budget

words.enDefinition: An amount or percentage used to decide which budget differences warrant reporting or investigation.

examples.en: The class set a variance threshold so its practice report would focus on the largest unexplained differences.
examples.zh: 全班设定了「差异关注阈值」，让练习报告集中在尚未解释的大额差异上。

examples.en: The repair line exceeded the variance threshold when we expressed its small difference as a percentage.
examples.zh: 维修项目的金额差异不大，但换算成百分比后就超出了「差异关注阈值」。

words.enDefinition: A report highlighting results outside defined limits or target ranges so they can be reviewed.

examples.en: The exception report highlighted only the supply lines whose variance exceeded the threshold in our worksheet.
examples.zh: 「异常事项报告」只标出了练习表中差异超过阈值的物料项目。

examples.en: We prepared an exception report when the practice theatre's cleaning expenses went outside the agreed range.
examples.zh: 案例中剧场清洁费用超出约定范围后，我们编制了「异常事项报告」。

collocations: flag unusual costs in an exception report

words.enDefinition: An approach in which managers focus on significant departures from plans or expected limits.

examples.en: Management by exception kept the class discussion focused on unexpected labour costs and the unusually low sales.
examples.zh: 「例外管理」让课堂讨论集中在意外的人工成本以及异常偏低的销量上。

examples.en: In the exercise, management by exception meant checking flagged figures before reviewing small routine differences.
examples.zh: 在练习中，「例外管理」意味着先查被标记的数字，再看例行的小额差异。

collocations: apply management by exception to budget review
an example of management by exception

words.enDefinition: The person assigned to investigate a reported variance and explain or coordinate follow-up on it.

examples.en: We named a variance owner for the unplanned rental charge so one person could check the invoices.
examples.zh: 我们为这笔未计划的租赁费指定了「差异跟进责任人」，由一人去核查发票。

examples.en: The variance owner reported that the difference came from a late delivery billed in the following month.
examples.zh: 「差异跟进责任人」指出，这项差异来自一次晚到、在次月入账的送货。

collocations: ask the variance owner for an update

words.enDefinition: Work done after a variance is flagged to confirm its cause and track any agreed response.

examples.en: The variance follow-up showed that the extra charge had been billed to the wrong class project.
examples.zh: 「差异跟进」发现，这笔额外收费记到了错误的课堂项目上。

examples.en: We moved the unresolved supply difference to the next meeting's agenda for variance follow-up and discussion.
examples.zh: 我们把尚未解决的物料差异列入下次会议议程，以便「差异跟进」和讨论。

words.enDefinition: An amount by which the actual cost of an activity or project exceeds the planned or estimated cost.

examples.en: A cost overrun appeared in the final repair worksheet when the practice workshop added a second inspection.
examples.zh: 模拟工场增加了第二次检查之后，最终维修练习表出现了「成本超支」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the cost overrun had come from higher prices or a larger order.
examples.zh: 老师问，「成本超支」是由于价格更高，还是因为订单量更大。

collocations: a cost overrun on a project

words.enDefinition: The amount by which expected or available resources fall short of what the budget needs to cover planned costs.

examples.en: The budget shortfall arose when the case assumed the project would receive less funding for campus workshops.
examples.zh: 案例预计校园工场项目获得的经费会减少，因此出现了「预算资金缺口」。

examples.en: We used the revised grant figure to estimate the budget shortfall before writing our classroom report.
examples.zh: 写课堂报告前，我们用修订后的资助金额估算了「预算资金缺口」。

collocations: explain the budget shortfall in the report

words.enDefinition: An amount spent in excess of the budget or other agreed spending limit.

examples.en: The print room recorded an overspend on paper after an unusually busy week of student orders.
examples.zh: 学生订单异常繁忙的一周过后，印刷室记录了一笔纸张费用「超支额」。

examples.en: The worksheet showed an overspend in the repair budget and traced it to two replacement parts.
examples.zh: 练习表显示维修预算有一笔「超支额」，并追溯到两个更换的零件。

words.enDefinition: An amount by which spending is below the budget or allocation for the period.

examples.en: The rehearsal hall reported an underspend after its planned equipment service was moved to the next month.
examples.zh: 原定的设备保养移到下个月后，排练厅列报了「低于预算的金额」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the underspend was temporary or reflected a lasting drop in maintenance costs.
examples.zh: 老师问，这笔「低于预算的金额」是暂时的，还是反映维修费用长期下降。

words.enDefinition: A difference between plan and outcome caused by an event not expected to repeat in the normal periods ahead.

examples.en: The one-off variance came from replacing a broken window in the practice workshop late in term.
examples.zh: 学期快结束时，模拟工场换了一扇坏窗，产生了「一次性差异」。

examples.en: We excluded the one-off variance when discussing the usual monthly cost of operating the rehearsal room.
examples.zh: 讨论排练室通常的月度运行成本时，我们剔除了这项「一次性差异」。

collocations: identify a one-off variance in spending

words.enDefinition: A difference that continues across reporting periods and may indicate an underlying change or issue.

examples.en: The report showed a persistent variance after three months of higher charges for the same quantity of paper.
examples.zh: 相同数量的纸连续三个月收费偏高，报告因此显示出「持续性差异」。

examples.en: A persistent variance in support hours prompted the class to recheck the assumptions in its exercise.
examples.zh: 支持服务工时出现「持续性差异」，这让同学们重新核对练习里的假设。

collocations: a persistent variance across several months

words.enDefinition: A difference arising because a planned income or expense item falls into a different budget period than expected.

examples.en: The tutor called it a budget timing variance because the planned service happened a month later.
examples.zh: 老师说这是「预算时间性差异」，因为原计划的服务晚了一个月才发生。

examples.en: A budget timing variance appeared in May and reversed when the planned service took place in June.
examples.zh: 五月出现了「预算时间性差异」，六月原定的服务实际发生后，这项差异随之抵消。

collocations: track the reversal of a budget timing variance

words.enDefinition: To combine separate spending and income plans from departments into a single budget for the organisation.

examples.en: Before the review meeting, our group had to consolidate departmental budgets for the three campus venues.
examples.zh: 评审会之前，我们小组得「汇总各部门预算」，把三个校园场地的预算合在一起。

examples.en: To consolidate departmental budgets, we checked that both teams had listed their shared cleaner's hours only once.
examples.zh: 为了「汇总各部门预算」，我们核对两个团队共用的清洁人员的工时是否只计了一次。

collocations: consolidate departmental budgets into a single plan
consolidate departmental budgets by spending category

words.enDefinition: Adherence to the spending limits, authorisations and other requirements of an approved budget.

examples.en: The case assigned budget compliance to the office manager, who checked workshop orders against approved spending categories.
examples.zh: 案例由行政经理负责「预算执行合规性」，核查工场订单是否属于经批准的支出类别。

examples.en: The review looked at budget compliance because two projects had moved spending between categories without approval.
examples.zh: 有两个项目未经批准就在不同类别之间调剂了支出，所以审查关注「预算执行合规性」。

collocations: check budget compliance before approving a purchase

words.enDefinition: The latest estimate of the total spending, income or balance expected at the end of a reporting period.

examples.en: The forecast outturn showed higher annual repair costs even though most of the current month's orders were unfinished.
examples.zh: 虽然本月大多数订单尚未完成，「预计期末执行结果」已显示全年维修成本会上升。

examples.en: Each department updated its forecast outturn after learning what it had already spent during the first term.
examples.zh: 各部门了解第一学期已经花了多少后，都更新了「预计期末执行结果」。

collocations: compare the forecast outturn with budget

words.enDefinition: Recorded revenues, costs or other results from the start of the financial year through the latest reporting date.

examples.en: We compared year-to-date actuals with the budget for the same six months in the finance exercise.
examples.zh: 在财务练习中，我们把「年初至今实际数」和同一六个月的预算进行比较。

examples.en: The year-to-date actuals showed that the workshop had already used most of its annual materials allowance.
examples.zh: 「年初至今实际数」显示，工场已用掉年度材料定额的大部分。

collocations: reconcile year-to-date actuals to the ledger

words.enDefinition: The part of an amount set aside for a specific purpose that has not yet been spent.

examples.en: The case showed an unspent allocation for training because the last workshop had been moved to spring.
examples.zh: 最后一场培训改在春季举行，因此案例中的培训经费还有「尚未使用的拨款」。

examples.en: At the review, we listed the unspent allocation separately from funds already committed to confirmed orders.
examples.zh: 评审时，我们把「尚未使用的拨款」和已经为确定订单承诺的款项分别列出。

words.zhGloss: 预算与最新预测的比较
words.enDefinition: A comparison of the approved plan with the latest estimate of where the period's results will end up.
acceptedZhAnswers: 预算与最新预测的比较

examples.en: The budget-to-forecast comparison showed that recent paper price changes could put the print room above its spending plan.
examples.zh: 「预算与最新预测的比较」显示，最近纸价的变化可能使印刷室开支超出计划。

examples.en: Our group used a budget-to-forecast comparison to explain why the annual repairs estimate had changed since approval.
examples.zh: 我们组用「预算与最新预测的比较」，解释年度维修费估计为何在预算批准后发生变化。

collocations: show expected changes in a budget-to-forecast comparison
